title: Pakistan government weighs emergency rule in PTI-held KP amid ongoing crisis
detail: Pakistan's federal government is seriously considering imposing emergency rule under Article 232 or governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), the political stronghold of imprisoned former PM Imran Khan and his PTI party. Federal ministers including Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry cited the provincial government's handling of terrorism and the breakdown of talks with PTI as justification. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi stated governor's rule and emergency are 'final options' pending presidential and prime ministerial approval. JUI-F chief Fazal ur Rehman advised against the move. PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar warned of strong resistance to any such imposition.

media.caption: Federal minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry warns KP chief minister's conduct paves the way for emergency rule imposition

title: Official says governor's rule in KP could last until elections
detail: Ikhtiar Wali Khan, the PM's coordinator on information for KP, said governor's rule would remain 'as long as necessary' and could continue until the elections. He said CM Sohail Afridi is in protective custody after surrendering voluntarily, and that the provincial assembly was not functioning. The President approved emergency and governor's rule on Oct 11 under Articles 232 and 234 on the PM's advice, citing terrorism and security threats. PTI rejects the account.

media.caption: Ikhtiar Wali Khan, PM's coordinator on information for KP
